identity.title: Monitoring of 3C 286 with ALMA, IRAM, and SMA from 2006 to 2025: Stability, Synchrotron Ages, and Frequency-dependent Polarization Attributed to Core-shift

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present the results of multi-frequency monitoring of the radio quasar 3C 286, conducted using three instruments: ALMA at 91.5, 103.5, 233.0, and 343.4 GHz, the IRAM 30-m Telescope at 86 and 229 GHz, and SMA at 225 GHz.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00001.CAL.

question.value: To determine the long-term stability of the total flux, fractional polarization, and electric vector position angle (EVPA) of the calibrator quasar 3C 286 at millimeter and submillimeter wavelengths, and test models of synchrotron cooling and core-shift.

evidence.quote: In this paper, we present the result of polarimetric observations of 3C 286 using ALMA, IRAM, and SMA at 91.5–343.4 GHz, spanning from October 2006 to February 2025.
The combined data from these three monitoring programs allows for a precise investigation of the stability and properties of 3C 286 at millimeter and submillimeter wavelengths.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00001.CAL.

The data has been primarily obtained in Band 3 (91.5 and 103.5 GHz) and Band 7 (343.4 GHz) since May 2018. Data in Band 6 (233.0 GHz) has been obtained less frequently as a complement to the Band 7 data

findings_qualitative.value: The total flux of 3C 286 has remained stable up to 229 GHz over 2006-2024; the apparent decrease of 2-15% seen in ALMA data is partially due to the unmodeled brightening of Uranus (up to 4%) and possibly other instrumental/atmospheric factors.

evidence.quote: The IRAM measurements from 2006 to 2024 show that the total flux of 3C 286 is stable within measurement uncertainties, indicating long-term stability up to 229 GHz, when applying a fixed Kelvin-to-Jansky conversion factor throughout its dataset.

ALMA data from 2018 to 2024 exhibit a decrease in flux, which up to 4% could be attributed to an apparent increase in the absolute brightness of Uranus, the primary flux calibrator for ALMA with the ESA4 model.

findings_qualitative.value: EVPA and fractional polarization are stable across all millimeter/submillimeter observing frequencies over the 20-year period.

evidence.quote: The polarization properties of 3C 286 are stable across all observing frequencies.
Likewise, long-term monitoring observations with ALMA and IRAM suggest that both EVPA and fractional polarization of 3C 286 have remained nearly constant over the last $\sim$20 years.

findings_qualitative.value: The EVPA rotation and increasing Faraday RM with frequency are consistent with core-shift in a Blandford & Konigl conical jet, accompanied by reduced Faraday depolarization at shorter wavelengths.

evidence.quote: The Faraday rotation measure increases as a function of frequency up to $\rm (3.2\pm1.5)\times10^4\ rad\ m^{-2}$, following $\mid$RM$\mid\propto \nu$^$\alpha$^ with $\alpha=2.05\pm0.06$. This trend is consistent with the core-shift effect expected in a conical jet.

claims.hypothesis: The intrinsic millimeter/submillimeter total flux of 3C 286 is stable over multi-year baselines.
claims.experiment: Long-term monitoring with IRAM (2006-2024 at 86 and 229 GHz) and ALMA (2018-2024 at 91.5-343.4 GHz) combined with analysis of Uranus calibration variations.
claims.result: IRAM measurements show constant flux within uncertainties (change of -2% at 86 GHz and +9% at 229 GHz), while ALMA apparent declines (2% to 15%) can be partially explained by a ~4% brightening of Uranus.
claims.finding: The intrinsic total flux of 3C 286 has remained stable up to 229 GHz over the 20-year period.

evidence.quote: Taken together, these results suggest that the intrinsic total flux of 3C 286 has remained stable up to 229 GHz over the monitoring period.

claims.hypothesis: The EVPA of 3C 286 gradually rotates as a function of frequency due to core-shift in a conical jet.
claims.experiment: Fit EVPA values from 5 GHz to 343.4 GHz with a single power-law function of wavelength squared and derive the frequency-dependent RM.
claims.result: RM increases from 23 rad m^-2 to 3.2 x 10^4 rad m^-2 in the rest frame, scaling as nu^a with a = 2.05 +/- 0.06.
claims.finding: The observed frequency-dependent EVPA rotation is consistent with the core-shift effect predicted by the Blandford & Konigl conical jet model where a = 2.

evidence.loc: 4.3 EVPA rotation as a function of frequency
evidence.quote: The best-fit line represents $\mid$RM core,$\nu$\mid\propto \nu^{a}$ with the power-law index $a=2.05\pm0.06$, which is consistent with the theoretically expected value of $a=2$ for the BK conical jet model.

claims.hypothesis: The continuous increase in fractional polarization with frequency is driven by reduced Faraday depolarization at shorter wavelengths.
claims.experiment: Fit fractional polarization as a function of wavelength squared from 1.5 GHz to 343.4 GHz with a single power law.
claims.result: Fractional polarization follows log(m) = k' log(lambda^2) + C' with k' = -0.047 +/- 0.001 across four orders of magnitude in lambda^2.
claims.finding: Faraday depolarization decreases at shorter wavelengths because lambda^2 decreases much faster than RM increases.

evidence.quote: Although RM increases at shorter wavelengths, the magnitude of the increase in RM is smaller than the decrease in wavelength squared, resulting in a reduced depolarization effect.

why_this_data.value: Combining ALMA 7-m, IRAM 30-m, and SMA observations provides unprecedented frequency coverage (86 to 343.4 GHz) and time baseline (2006 to 2025) for high-accuracy millimeter/submillimeter polarimetry of a primary radio calibrator.

evidence.quote: In this paper, we present the result of polarimetric observations of 3C 286 using ALMA, IRAM, and SMA at 91.5–343.4 GHz, spanning from October 2006 to February 2025. The combined data from these three monitoring programs allows for a precise investigation

why_this_method.value: Stacking the stable polarimetric monitoring data allows derivation of reference EVPA and polarization fractions with sub-percent and sub-degree statistical uncertainties, resolving previously discordant millimeter measurements.

evidence.quote: This stability allows us to obtain the fractional polarization and EVPA values with unprecedented accuracy at millimeter/submillimeter wavelengths by stacking all the data.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Excluded historical SMA data before June 2022 because changes in solar system models and calibration inconsistencies introduced unquantified systematic flux offsets.

evidence.quote: However, we do not include these measurements in our analysis due to inconsistencies in the flux calibration process and transitions from older solar system models to the CASA-standard models during the monitoring.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Excluded MeerKAT 1.4 GHz EVPA (29.2 deg) from the RM calculation due to large frequency-dependent uncertainties up to 3 deg.

evidence.quote: We did not include $\chi=29.2^\circ$ at 1.4 GHz obtained with MeerKAT in the RM calculation, due to its frequency-dependent uncertainties of up to 3$^{\circ}$ (see Figure 2 in (cite: taylor24)).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Rejected a one-zone continuous injection synchrotron model for the entire source because it implies an apparent expansion speed (beta_app = 2.6) much faster than observed in the inner jet (beta_app = 0.6).

evidence.loc: 4.2 Synchrotron age and magnetic field strength
evidence.quote: However, these apparent speeds are significantly faster than the apparent speed $\beta_{\rm app}=0.6\pm0.5$ observed in the inner jet at 5 mas from the core (cite: an17).

evidence.loc: 4.2 Synchrotron age and magnetic field strength
evidence.quote: This discrepancy suggests that the spectrum may not represent the age of the entire jet, but instead may partially represent the age of electrons that were accelerated in situ as the jet propagates through the ambient medium.

limitations_admitted.value: The 4% brightening of Uranus cannot fully explain the >10% flux decrease observed in ALMA Bands 6 and 7, indicating additional unmodeled atmospheric or instrumental effects.

evidence.quote: Nevertheless, the change in the brightness of Uranus alone cannot fully account for the decreasing trend observed in the ALMA measurements, as the magnitudes of the decrease in Band 6 and 7 exceed 10%.

limitations_admitted.value: IRAM EVPA uncertainties at 229 GHz appear underestimated, given an average formal uncertainty of 5.1 deg versus an observed scatter of 9.6 deg.

evidence.quote: Moreover, the average of the EVPA uncertainties for IRAM at 229 GHz is 5.1$^{\circ}$, while the standard deviation of those measurements is 9.6$^{\circ}$. This discrepancy suggests that the EVPA uncertainties for IRAM may have been underestimated.

referee_caveats_inferred: ALMA calibration scans were taken with the 7-m compact array, potentially affected by elevation limits and transfer calibration uncertainties since 3C 286 peaks at low elevation (<37 deg).
Underlying jet sub-structure (C1 vs C2) is unresolved by the single-dish and compact interferometer beams, requiring multi-zone interpretation rather than a pure single-component jet.

reproducibility.score_reason: The ALMA calibration data and reduction pipeline (AMAPOLA) are public, and the analytical fitting functions (power-law regressions) are mathematically explicit. However, exact reproduction requires downloading hundreds of grid-calibrator execution blocks from 2018-2024 from project 2011.0.00001.CAL and combining them with external IRAM/SMA datasets.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The core finding—the reference EVPA and fractional polarization values for 3C 286 across ALMA bands—can be directly recalculated by downloading the ALMA 7-m calibration scans under 2011.0.00001.CAL and executing AMAPOLA.
